name: CR-Planner (Critic-guided planning with Retrieval-augmentation)
venue: ACL 2025 (Proceedings of the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, Long Papers, pp. 25589-25604). Preprint arXiv:2410.01428 (Oct 2024). Also reviewed on OpenReview (id=4JfFW7d1gu).
authors_affiliation: Xingxuan Li (MiroMind; Nanyang Technological University — work done mainly at DAMO Academy, Alibaba Group, under the Alibaba-NTU Joint PhD Program), Weiwen Xu (DAMO Academy, Alibaba Group; Hupan Lab, Hangzhou), Ruochen Zhao (NTU), Fangkai Jiao (NTU), Shafiq Joty (NTU; Salesforce Research), Lidong Bing (MiroMind, corresponding author). Lead/primary affiliations: MiroMind, NTU, DAMO Academy (Alibaba Group).
task_domain: Reasoning-heavy and domain-knowledge-intensive problem solving that couples reasoning with retrieval: competitive programming / code (USACO), theorem-driven math reasoning (TheoremQA-Math), and reasoning-intensive document retrieval (BRIGHT StackBio/StackEcon). Spans code, math QA, and retrieval/IR; cast as planning/decision-making over a {REASON, GENQUERY, RETRIEVE} action space.
problem_setting: Single-agent, interactive test-time planning framed as a Markov Decision Process (S, A_s, P, R, T). A state s_t is the action-observation history (o_0,a_0,...,o_t); observations are sub-goal types (REASON/GENQUERY/RETRIEVE) or execution outputs (RATIONALE/QUERY/DOC). At each step a policy pi(s_t)=argmax_a R(s_t,a) selects the action with highest expected reward, where R is estimated by fine-tuned critic models. A large general generator (GPT-4) produces candidates and a BM25 retriever produces documents; small fine-tuned critics (Skywork-Reward-Llama-3.1-8B) score them. Supervision: step-wise reward training data is collected offline via Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) over generator/retriever rollouts (no human step annotations; final-answer correctness / test-case signals drive MCTS simulation scoring). The base generator is NOT fine-tuned (plug-and-play with closed-source LLMs); only the external critics are trained. Inference is online step-by-step planning; the external knowledge corpus is fixed/static.
what_is_retrieved: External knowledge documents grounding the reasoning: for USACO, algorithm textbook chapters and a problem bank of other USACO problems; for TheoremQA-Math, processed documents from high-quality STEM datasets (GSM8K, GSM8K-RFT, MATH, AQuA-RAT, TheoremQA, CAMEL-MATH); for BRIGHT StackBio/StackEcon, web-derived StackExchange-cited documents/articles/tutorials. The retrieval action (RETRIEVE) returns DOC observations; the GENQUERY action produces search QUERY strings. No demos/cases/trajectories/skills are retrieved as reusable units — only knowledge documents.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus. Retrieval targets fixed, pre-gathered knowledge sources (USACO textbooks + problem bank; BRIGHT STEM document collections; StackExchange documents). The store does not grow during deployment, and the agent does not write experiences/cases back into a retrievable memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking. The RETRIEVE action surfaces top-k candidate documents (k=10 for the final retrieval in BRIGHT nDCG@10 evaluation; top-k candidates per Table 9), and the execution critic g^e_DOC ranks/selects among them. No notion of recovering a complete minimal evidence set; selection is critic-driven single-best (or top-10 for nDCG) rather than precision-driven variable-size.
retrieval_unit: Document (knowledge passage): a textbook chapter / problem-bank problem / STEM-corpus document / StackExchange-cited document, surfaced as a DOC observation. Query strings (GENQUERY->QUERY) are an intermediate conceptual-query unit, not a retrieved unit. Reasoning is at the rationale-step granularity (REASON->RATIONALE).
index_source: Static, offline-constructed store: benchmark-provided external corpora (USACO textbooks + full problem bank; BRIGHT processed STEM documents; StackExchange web content already gathered into BRIGHT). Indexed once and frozen; not online/test-time-induced and not hybrid.
index_structure_topology: Flat term-based (BM25/inverted-index) document store. No graph, hierarchy, or cluster/toolkit organization is described; documents are retrieved by lexical relevance to the generated query.
retriever_type: BM25 (sparse, term-based, off-the-shelf). The paper chooses BM25 for efficiency in both MCTS training-data collection and inference across all three domains. No dense/learned/generative retriever is trained; relevance selection among retrieved DOCs is delegated to the fine-tuned execution critic g^e_DOC rather than a learned dense retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: None for the retriever itself (off-the-shelf BM25, untrained). The learned signal lives in the CRITIC models, not the retriever: an execution critic g^e_DOC is trained (pairwise ranking loss, Burges 2005 / Ouyang 2022) on MCTS-collected, long-term-reward-labeled trajectories to select among BM25-retrieved documents, and the sub-goal critic g^g learns when RETRIEVE (vs REASON/GENQUERY) maximizes downstream task reward. So the effective retrieval/selection signal is downstream-task-effectiveness (MCTS-estimated long-term reward) realized through trained critics, not retriever contrastive training.
query_construction: Thought-conditioned synthetic query generation. When GENQUERY is selected, the generator (GPT-4) produces conceptual search queries derived from the current reasoning step/state; multiple (3) candidate queries are sampled via temperature sampling and the execution critic g^e_QUERY selects the best. Queries are required to be conceptual/relevant to the reasoning step and to avoid specific numbers/entities of that step (per the prompt). The first retrieval may also use the problem itself; subsequent queries are reasoning-conditioned.
query_granularity: Step/state-level. A query is constructed per planning step when GENQUERY is chosen (conditioned on the current RATIONALE/state), not once at t=0. Retrieval is interleaved across steps, so queries are formed at the reasoning-step granularity within the trajectory.
when_to_retrieve: Adaptive (learned router) + iterative. WHEN to retrieve is decided at every step by the sub-goal critic g^g, which scores REASON vs GENQUERY vs RETRIEVE and routes to the highest-reward action; retrieval can occur multiple times across a trajectory (iterative) and only when the critic judges it beneficial (not a fixed schedule).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Learned critic reward score (a trained sub-goal critic g^g acting as a learned router). At each state the sub-goal critic assigns reward scores to {REASON, GENQUERY, RETRIEVE}; RETRIEVE (or GENQUERY) is triggered when its critic score is highest. The critic is trained on MCTS-estimated long-term rewards, so the trigger is a learned-complexity/utility signal rather than token confidence, attention, or reflection tokens.
reranking: Yes, via the execution critic acting as a learned reranker/selector. For RETRIEVE, BM25 returns top-k candidate DOCs and the fine-tuned execution critic g^e_DOC scores each (first-logit reward) and selects the optimal document — a critic-based reranking stage rather than a cross-encoder/RRF reranker. (For nDCG@10 evaluation the top-10 are kept.)
retrieved_context_refinement: Critic-based selection/filtering: among the top-k retrieved DOCs the execution critic picks the most useful one (distractor/irrelevant-document filtering), and the sub-goal critic can choose to REASON again over a retrieved doc (e.g., decide retrieval is insufficient and trigger a second-level retrieval). No compression, summarization, or decompose-then-recompose; refinement is per-step critic-driven selection plus optional reasoning-over-documents.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation within an iterative plan. The selected DOC is appended to the action-observation history (state) and conditions subsequent REASON steps and the final generator answer/code; retrieved knowledge grounds rationales to improve factuality. Critic scores are used as a search/selection signal (not injected into the prompt). Retrieved content is used as in-context grounding, not as a training signal or latent token.
planning_integration: Per-step interleaved critic-guided planning over a {REASON, GENQUERY, RETRIEVE} action space (retrieve-and-reason interleaving). At inference the framework alternates Sub-Goal Selection (critic g^g picks the next sub-goal) and Execution Selection (critic g^e picks the best sampled candidate), forming a step-by-step plan; MCTS is used OFFLINE only to collect critic-training data (it explores action sequences and back-propagates long-term rewards), not at inference. (A 'Vanilla MCTS at inference' variant is studied as a baseline and underperforms CR-Planner.)
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-CoT-step / per-sub-goal: retrieval (and query generation) is woven in at the granularity of individual reasoning sub-goals within a trajectory — each step the planner may REASON, GENQUERY, or RETRIEVE, so search is interleaved per reasoning step rather than per final answer or per token.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw free-text knowledge document (textbook chapter / problem-bank problem / STEM passage / StackExchange document) injected verbatim into the planning state/prompt. Not distilled into a strategy/guideline, workflow, executable skill, or latent token.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw knowledge document / passage (concrete reference content). Not a distilled strategy/insight, state-aware guideline, reusable workflow, or procedural skill — though queries are deliberately made conceptual, the retrieved unit itself is raw document text.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Fine-tuned critic models as the central noise guard: the execution critic g^e_DOC filters out irrelevant/misleading retrieved documents by scoring usefulness, and the sub-goal critic can decline retrieval (route to REASON) when retrieval is unhelpful, directly attacking the 'retrieving error / irrelevant retrieval' failure mode. The reason-then-retrieve interleaving and conceptual-query constraint also reduce off-topic retrieval. No retriever-aware SFT of the base model and no reflection-token mechanism.
memory_type: none (no persistent cross-task experience memory). The framework relies on a static external knowledge corpus plus trained critic models; it does not maintain an episodic/skill/workflow memory that is read and written during deployment. The MCTS-collected trajectories are training data for critics, not a queryable memory.
write_back: False. The system does not store new experiences/cases/skills into a retrievable memory at test time. MCTS trajectories are collected offline once to train critics; nothing is written back during inference.
online_growth: No. The retrievable knowledge store is frozen after offline construction and does not grow at deployment/test time.
write_back_trigger: never (no write-back to a retrievable memory). Offline, MCTS produces pairwise (chosen, rejected) preference data used solely to train the critic models; this is training-data generation, not test-time memory writing.
failure_experience_usage: Indirect, success-vs-suboptimal contrastive at TRAINING time only: MCTS yields pairwise data where a chosen observation (highest long-term-reward score) is contrasted against a rejected sibling observation (lower score) sharing the same parent, and critics are trained via pairwise ranking loss on these (chosen, rejected) pairs. So suboptimal/failed action branches inform critic training contrastively, but failed experiences are not stored or retrieved at inference.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (no persistent memory store is mutated). Critic models are trained once on the MCTS-collected dataset (no online update of a memory). [uncertain] whether any iterative re-collection of MCTS data is performed beyond a single round.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Yes (partially): the decision of whether/when to RETRIEVE and which retrieved DOC to keep is governed by LEARNED critic models (sub-goal critic g^g and execution critic g^e_DOC) trained on MCTS-estimated long-term rewards via pairwise ranking — i.e., a learned selection/routing policy rather than fixed similarity top-k. The underlying retriever (BM25) is itself fixed; the learned policy sits at the action-selection/reranking layer (value/reward-based selection, not RL-finetuned retriever).
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private setting; no sharing of memory/experience across multiple agents or heterogeneous frameworks. (The trained critic models are reusable plug-and-play across different base generators — GPT-4, Claude-3.5, Llama-3.1 — but this is critic portability across base LLMs, not cross-agent experience sharing.)
benchmarks: USACO (USA Computing Olympiad competitive-programming benchmark; 123 bronze, 100 silver, 63 gold, 21 platinum problems; Shi et al. 2024); TheoremQA-Math (206 solvable theorem-driven math problems, the Math subset of TheoremQA rewritten in BRIGHT; Chen et al. 2023 / Su et al. 2024); BRIGHT StackBio and StackEcon (103 biology + 103 economics reasoning-intensive retrieval questions from StackExchange; Su et al. 2024).
benchmark_family: code (USACO — competitive programming / Olympiad), QA-math (TheoremQA-Math — theorem-driven math reasoning), and reasoning-intensive retrieval/IR (BRIGHT StackBio/StackEcon). Cross-cutting: knowledge-intensive + reasoning-heavy benchmarks.
baselines: Standard prompting (Ouyang et al. 2022); Chain-of-Thought (CoT, Wei et al. 2022); Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023); standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG, Lewis et al. 2020); Chain-of-Knowledge (CoK, Li et al. 2024, SoTA CoT+retrieval-with-rationale-postedit); Retrieval+Reflexion (from Shi et al. 2024, USACO) reported on USACO; BM25 baseline for BRIGHT retrieval; Claude-3.5 zero-shot for BRIGHT. Additional analysis baselines: Vanilla MCTS at inference; LoRA-fine-tuned Llama-3.1-70B base model on the same MCTS data; GPT-4 (in-context) as critic; single unified critic vs task-specific critics. Self-RAG is explicitly excluded as a baseline because it requires fine-tuning the base model.
key_metrics: USACO: Pass@1 (%) overall and per difficulty tier (Bronze/Silver/Gold/Platinum). TheoremQA-Math: accuracy (%). BRIGHT StackBio/StackEcon: nDCG@10. Improvements reported as absolute percentage-point gains over baselines.
headline_result: CR-Planner outperforms the baseline by 10.06% on average across the three tasks (key contribution claim). On USACO Pass@1 it reaches 17.59% overall vs 10.10% standard prompting (+7.49 pts) and beats CoT 12.38, RAG 8.47, CoK 8.14; CR-Planner+Reflexion reaches 22.80% overall (vs Retrieval+Reflexion 18.05). On TheoremQA-Math, 53.40% vs 39.81% standard (+13.59 pts). On BRIGHT, nDCG@10 improves over BM25 by +10.31 on StackBio and +7.9 on StackEcon.
ablations: (1) Fine-tuned critics vs GPT-4-as-critic (Fig 3): fine-tuned domain-specific critics beat GPT-4 in-context critics, especially on domain-specific StackBio, validating domain fine-tuning. (2) Various base generators (Table 4): CR-Planner improves Claude-3.5 by 4.56% and Llama-3.1-70B by 2.61% (smaller than the 7.49% GPT-4 gain, since critics were trained on GPT-4 data) — shows plug-and-play across open/closed models. (3) Fine-tuning critics vs fine-tuning the base model (Table 5, TheoremQA-Math): LoRA-fine-tuned Llama-3.1 reaches 34.10 (> Standard 31.43) but CR-Planner reaches 38.62, i.e., training external critics beats fine-tuning the base model and costs less. (4) Retrieve-or-not (Table 6, USACO): CR-Planner w/o Retrieval 14.33 vs full CR-Planner 17.59 vs Standard 10.10 — retrieval contributes ~3.3 pts; reasoning critic alone already helps. (5) Vanilla MCTS at inference (Table 7, USACO): 12.42 vs CR-Planner 17.59 — learned critics beat raw test-time MCTS (which overfits to local test cases). (6) Execution sampling count (Fig 4): gains rise sharply from 1->2 candidates, converge ~3; 3 chosen for main experiments. (7) Single-unified vs task-specific critics (Table 8, USACO): task-specific 17.59 vs single unified 12.38 — task-specific critics generalize better.
evaluation_decoupling: Partially decoupled by task: for the BRIGHT StackBio/StackEcon retrieval tasks an intrinsic retrieval metric (nDCG@10) is reported, separate from the end-to-end task metrics (Pass@1 on USACO, accuracy on TheoremQA-Math). There is no per-step Recall@k / completeness metric isolating the retriever from the end-to-end pipeline within the code/math tasks; the retrieval-or-not ablation (Table 6) indirectly isolates retrieval's end-to-end contribution.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome metrics (Pass@1, accuracy, nDCG@10). Process quality is examined qualitatively and via ablations rather than a dedicated step-wise score: Fig 3 (critic quality), Fig 4 (execution-sampling effect), and the Vanilla-MCTS / retrieve-or-not / unified-vs-task-specific-critic analyses probe intermediate selection quality, but no formal reasoning-faithfulness or step-wise retrieval-accuracy metric is reported.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Generator decoding temperature 0.7 with exactly 3 sampled candidates per execution (chosen to balance performance/cost; gains converge at ~3 per Fig 4). BM25 chosen over dense retrieval specifically for efficiency in both MCTS data collection and inference. The framework trains only small 8B critics (LoRA) rather than fine-tuning the base model, which the paper notes requires less computation than full base-model fine-tuning; MCTS-based offline data collection adds training-time overhead vs in-context baselines (acknowledged). Critics distill MCTS guidance into cheap plug-and-play scorers. [uncertain] no explicit per-query latency, token-count, dollar-cost, or MCTS-rollout-count numbers are reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed selection counts: 3 candidate executions sampled per sub-goal (RATIONALE/QUERY via temperature sampling; DOC via top-k) with the execution critic choosing 1; for BRIGHT the final retrieval keeps top-10 documents (to match nDCG@10). No adaptive/precision-driven k and no explicit token/prompt budget cap is reported. [uncertain] exact top-k used for intermediate DOC candidate sampling and the prompt token budget.
builds_on: Chain-of-Thought (Wei et al. 2022) and RAG (Lewis et al. 2020) as the reason+retrieve foundation; process-supervision / planning-based reasoning (Lightman et al. 2024 'Let's verify step by step'; RAP-style reward estimation; Jiao et al. 2024 planning-based reasoning via DPO on process-reward-ranked trajectories); Monte Carlo Tree Search (Browne et al. 2012) for trajectory simulation and long-term reward estimation; learning-to-rank pairwise ranking loss (Burges et al. 2005) and RLHF-style reward modeling (Ouyang et al. 2022); Skywork-Reward-Llama-3.1-8B reward model + LoRA (Hu et al. 2021); GPT-4 / Claude-3.5 / Llama-3.1 generators; BM25 retriever.
contrasts_with: Self-RAG (Asai et al. 2024) and variants (CRAG/Yan et al. 2024, Open-RAG/Islam et al. 2024) — which fine-tune the base LLM with reflection tokens to decide when/how to retrieve; CR-Planner instead trains external critics and leaves the base model untouched (works with closed-source LLMs). Chain-of-Knowledge (Li et al. 2024) and ReAct/Verify-and-Edit-style step-wise RAG that optimize retrieval sub-tasks locally (pre-retrieval analysis, query gen, doc selection) rather than learning global step rewards. Self-ask (Press et al. 2023), RePlug (Shi et al. 2023, fine-tuned retriever), Reflexion (linguistic-feedback self-correction). Also contrasts with applying Vanilla MCTS at inference (overfits to local test cases) and with fine-tuning the base model on the same data.
lineage: Group C (RAG + LLM planning). Sits in the lineage of critic/reward-guided step-wise reasoning-and-retrieval planners: it generalizes iterative RAG (FLARE/IRCoT/Self-RAG style 'when-to-retrieve') by replacing reflection-token / confidence triggers with trained sub-goal+execution critics over a unified {REASON, GENQUERY, RETRIEVE} action space, and combines this with MCTS-collected process rewards (RAP / 'Let's verify step by step' lineage). Distinct from experience/case-memory planners in that retrieval grounds against a static knowledge corpus and no episodic memory is written; the learned component is the critic policy, not the retriever or the base model.
code_url: https://github.com/xingxuanli/CR-Planner (URL stated in the paper; as of this writing the repo returns HTTP 404 — likely made private, renamed, or removed) [uncertain]
maintained_repo_url: N/A (single-paper code repo, not a continuously-maintained leaderboard/paper-list).
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A — not framed as case-based reasoning. If force-mapped: a weak Retrieve phase (BM25 documents, not cases) and no Reuse-as-adaptation/Revise/Retain. Flags: [Retrieve=partial(documents,not-cases), Reuse=no, Revise=no, Retain=no].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False: the paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. It retrieves knowledge documents, not prior solved cases as adaptable units.
tool_document_engineering: N/A — no tools/APIs are retrieved; the retrieved items are knowledge documents. Documents are used as-is (no synthetic-query augmentation/expanded summaries/weighted-field embeddings of the corpus); queries (not documents) are engineered to be conceptual.
index_content_separation: N/A / No: a single flat BM25 document index is used; there is no lightweight-index-then-heavy-content progressive-disclosure separation.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A — not a tool-use method; no live tool index, no RapidAPI/RESTful/MCP/function-calling protocol or CRUD auto-sync. The document corpus is static.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A — no inter-tool dependency modeling; not a tool-use method.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not CBR). Retrieved documents are used verbatim as in-context grounding; the closest mechanism is critic-guided selection/revision of which rationale/query/document to keep at each step (critic-guided revision of the plan), but there is no case-adaptation pipeline.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (this is a method/empirical paper, not a survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (not a benchmark-contribution paper). For context, evaluation reuses existing benchmarks: USACO (307 problems: 123 bronze/100 silver/63 gold/21 platinum), TheoremQA-Math (206 solvable problems), BRIGHT StackBio (103) and StackEcon (103) StackExchange questions with gold = documents cited in answers. External corpora: USACO 30 human-written textbook chapters + full problem bank; BRIGHT STEM document collection (GSM8K, GSM8K-RFT, MATH, AQuA-RAT, TheoremQA, CAMEL-MATH).
